meta.title: Thai C1 Advanced
meta.subtitle: 1500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Thai → English (see the Thai, recall the meaning) and English → Thai (see an English meaning, recall the Thai). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1500 words for an advanced learner, aligned to C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts, and recognise implicit meaning' — a learner here is able to express ideas fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions, to use language flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes, and to produce clear, well-structured, detailed text on complex subjects. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Thai, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 340 of the 1500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — philosophy and ethics, Buddhism and the inner life, academic and scholarly Thai, government, diplomacy and the constitution, the economy and development, medicine and the body, law and rights, language, linguistics and literature, the shades of feeling and judgement, the Pali- and Sanskrit-derived abstract nouns and adjectives of formal prose, the royal vocabulary (rachasap), and the literary connectors and adverbs — and the other 1160 are the commonest remaining words of Thai, taken from the word counts of the Thai National Corpus, a large collection of written Thai. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in Thai script with a romanisation beneath it in the Paiboon system, which marks the TONE on every syllable — no mark for mid, à low, â falling, á high, ǎ rising — because a Thai word said on the wrong tone is a different word; the Thai Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script and the rules that decide a tone. 136 nouns show the classifier they are counted with (a house is counted in หลัง, an animal in ตัว), and there are no forms to learn: Thai words never change shape. Example sentences come with 315 of the 1500 words, three apiece for 100 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, romanisation, classifiers and some example sentences: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: the Thai National Corpus word list as distributed by PyThaiNLP (CC0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
